facts.text: Terminology used consistently below: a **partition** is a group of documents sharing a compound key; a **generated document** is a document `$densify` synthesizes; the **densify field** is the field named in `$densify.field`.

3. The documents `$densify` generates contain only the values of `field` and of `partitionByFields`; every other field is absent. Consequence: a downstream `$project`, `$group`, or chart binding that expects a metadata field on every document will see it missing on generated rows unless `$fill` (or `$set`) puts it back. — <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify/>, <https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-how-to-use-densify-and-fill-with-time-series-in-mongodb/view>

12. Documents generated by `$densify` contain only the densified `field` and the fields named in `partitionByFields`. They carry no `_id` and none of the other fields of the surrounding documents. Any metadata not lifted into `partitionByFields` is lost for synthetic rows, and downstream stages that assume `_id` exists will misbehave. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify/

16. `$fill` with `method: "locf"` leaves `null` and missing values that appear *before* the first non-null value in sort order as `null`. Leading gaps at the start of a partition are never filled. If a partition contains only null or missing values, `locf` sets the field to `null` for the whole partition. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/fill/

This report covers the internal mechanism of MongoDB's two gap-filling aggregation stages, `$densify` and `$fill`: their desugaring into other stages, their execution state machine, their configuration surface, their invariants, and their documented and observed limits.

The working pipeline order is `$match` (narrow the range and the partitions) → `$densify` (create the missing instants) → `$fill` (give them values) → `$sort` (for output). `$densify` must precede `$fill`, because `$fill` only assigns values to documents that already exist. — <https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-how-to-use-densify-and-fill-with-time-series-in-mongodb/view>

**S3.** MongoDB states the division in its own words: "The $densify stage creates new documents to eliminate the gaps in the time or numeric domain at the required granularity level, and $fill sets values for the fields when a value is null or missing." **[converged: M A3, H 11, P 1]** — <https://www.mongodb.com/blog/post/introducing-gap-filling-time-series-data-mongodb-5-3>
